problem_type: canvas renderer migration geometry and interaction parity drift
symptom: After React Flow became the active canvas renderer, loaded-node fitting could use stale persisted geometry, selected image-like nodes lost the previous left and right magnetic plus affordances, connection endpoints appeared detached from cards, React Flow resize dots became visible, and edge colors or menus no longer matched the established Nomi interaction.
direct_cause: The migration moved node transforms, handles, resizing, edges, and viewport focus to React Flow but initially projected only persistent node data and accepted library-default handle, resize, and edge presentation. The previous renderer's transient appear/focus state and visual-size contract were not carried through one explicit adapter boundary.
class_root: Renderer replacement had no class-wide parity contract joining the Zustand model truth, rendered node geometry, transient visual state, connection affordances, endpoint geometry, resize presentation, and edge feedback, so individually working React Flow primitives could silently delete existing user interactions.
affected_population: Users fitting, focusing, selecting, connecting, resizing, or navigating image, video, asset, card, clip, and generated-result nodes
Users reopening media nodes whose rendered preview dimensions differ from their stored base size
Users of constrained windows and large canvases where viewport fitting, virtualization, and edge endpoints depend on exact rendered bounds
entry_points: Zustand nodes and edges projected into the active React Flow renderer
Fit, focus, restored-viewport visibility, minimap, virtualization, selection, and derived-node placement geometry
Selected image-like node connection drag from either magnetic plus affordance
Connection endpoint selection, resize controls, edge selection, and edge-mode menu feedback
New-node appearance and focused-variant flash state
internal_only_reason: React Flow supplies rendering primitives, but Nomi's established affordances, palette, geometry, transient feedback, and Zustand ownership are product invariants defined by repository code and real Electron journeys. An upstream version cannot decide or restore those application-specific contracts.
invariants: React Flow is the only canvas interaction and transform kernel while Zustand remains the business and persistence source of truth.
Every screen-space consumer and React Flow node or edge projection uses resolveNodeVisualSize for the same node state.
The adapter projects appear and focusFlash without copying business ownership into React Flow, and only nodes whose visual state changes receive a new projection object.
Geometry assertions that require stable card bounds wait for the finite appear lifecycle to finish; they do not misclassify the intentional 340ms scale animation as persistent double positioning.

A singly selected image-like node exposes left and right 29px magnetic plus affordances; ordinary nodes retain compact dots, hidden target handles contribute geometry without visible duplicate balls, and React Flow compatibility styles do not suppress the existing left and right magnetic plus affordances on collapsed group cards.
Completed edges terminate on the rendered left or right card boundary, use the Nomi accent palette, and retain the established 12px edge label plus Chevron, Check, and Scissors feedback.
React Flow resize controls retain their hit areas but do not introduce visible library-default dots or borders.
generality_proof: All active nodes and edges enter through toGenerationFlowNodes and toGenerationFlowEdges before React Flow renders them. Those projections resolve visual size, side-specific handles, incident state, and transient state for every node kind; GenerationFlowNodeView and GenerationFlowEdgeView then own the active-node handle, resize, edge, and menu implementation, while collapsed group projections retain their existing shared MagneticConnectionHandle surface outside the React Flow node shell. The geometry matrix covers fit, focus, visibility, virtualization, selection, and derived placement; the structure contract prevents compatibility CSS from escaping the node shell; and real Electron journeys check active-node and collapsed-group magnetic sides, hidden resize visuals, sub-two-pixel endpoint attachment, palette, label size, and icons rather than one fixture or node id.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Project Zustand-owned nodes and edges into one React Flow view model with renderer-aligned size, handle side, selection, incident, and transient visual state.
Render the only active connection, resize, edge, label, and edge-menu interaction surfaces from the adapter contract.
Resolve the renderer-aligned footprint shared by full nodes, React Flow projections, viewport commands, hit testing, and derived placement.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Every active React Flow node receives resolveNodeVisualSize, and every edge chooses source and target sides from the same visual centers.
Focus recovery centers from resolveNodeVisualSize and projects the restored 1400ms focus feedback through adapter visual state.
Large-canvas virtualization uses the same visual footprint, including media-derived height at the buffered viewport boundary.
Selection and placement resolve the rendered footprint instead of reading stale persisted dimensions.
Both connection sides, target geometry, resize hit areas, edge palette, and menu icons are rendered in one active kernel and exercised by the real journey.

recurrence.reason: Every renderer migration or new node kind can preserve data while dropping transient state, geometry, or interaction feedback; without one parity boundary the same regression can recur independently in fit, focus, handles, resize, edges, or menus.
same_class_scan: Scanned every generation-canvas size read, fit/focus consumer, React Flow node and edge projection, handle implementation, resize implementation, and legacy edge layer.
Compared the active React Flow renderer with the previous magnetic-handle, appearance, focus, edge palette, label, and menu behavior instead of checking only component presence.

Exercised image and video nodes through real selection, two-sided affordance inspection, connection creation, endpoint geometry, deselection, incident labels, and node dragging in the production Electron build.

prevention.invariant: Every active canvas node and edge is derived from Zustand state through one renderer projection that carries renderer-aligned geometry and all transient visual state required by the single React Flow kernel.
prevention.failure_mode: Adapter and visual-contract tests fail on omitted geometry or transient fields, TypeScript fails on incompatible projection data, and the real Electron journey fails when visible affordances, endpoint attachment, resize presentation, palette, or menu feedback diverge.
prevention.strategy: Keep persistent state in Zustand, centralize React Flow view projection and connection-affordance decisions, render one handle/resize/edge surface, and bind migration parity to both class-level tests and rendered geometry evidence.

legacy_paths.rationale: The target main branch had already removed the legacy canvas kernel and CanvasEdgeLayer before this merge. This change migrates the PR's geometry work into the existing React Flow adapter and restores renderer parity without adding or retaining a second callable renderer path.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The installed @xyflow/react 12.11.5 already exposes the required node, edge, handle, resize, and viewport APIs. The failures were omissions in Nomi's migration adapter and styling contract; upgrading the library would not define Nomi's magnetic affordance, palette, or Zustand ownership and would add unrelated risk.

migration: No project-data rewrite is required. Existing nodes and edges remain in the Zustand schema and are projected at read time through the React Flow adapter. The previous renderer kernel and edge layer are removed; transient appearance and focus state are recomputed in memory, and existing persisted sizes are interpreted through resolveNodeVisualSize.
residual_risks: DOM overlays outside node bounds still require separate viewport-collision tests because they are intentionally not part of the persisted node footprint.

Touch-only connection gestures and platform-specific accessibility zoom are not covered by the current mouse-based Electron journey and remain candidates for dedicated journeys when those inputs are supported.
